mainTopic: Two explanations of מותר נסכים, and which offerings need נסכים, with the sources in the פסוק
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's explanation of מותר נסכים (leftover libations): extra flour the הקדש gains when a supplier's price drops. Then the גמרא brings one ברייתא supporting רבי חייא בר יוסף, who said it is the overflow of the measuring cups. A second ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן and links its case directly to the משנה. Next, a new משנה teaches that all animal offerings need נסכים except בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם. The חטאת and אשם of a מצורע are an exception to that exception, since they do need נסכים. A ברייתא then finds each part of this rule in the פסוקים of במדבר 15. The main test is whether the type of offering can come as a נדר or a נדבה, and required holiday עולות and שלמים are also included. רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן disagree about which words leave out a bird עולה. The amud ends with the גמרא starting to explain why רבי יונתן needs a פסוק despite his 'יחדו' rule, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When the price drops, the supplier still gives at the better rate for the Temple
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the rule רבי יוחנן relies on. A supplier who agreed to sell at three סאה per סלע must give four סאה per סלע if the price drops, because the הקדש always gets the better deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he agreed to supply at three [סאה per סלע] and the price fell to four, he supplies at four, because the Temple treasury has the upper hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the rule behind רבי יוחנן's explanation of 'leftover libations'. If flour gets cheaper after the deal, the supplier must still give the Temple the new, cheaper rate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The supplier promised flour at 3 סאה for a סלע. Later the market drops to 4 סאה for a סלע, so he must give 4. The הקדש now ends up with more flour than it needs, and that extra is what רבי יוחנן calls 'leftover libations'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple treasury has the upper hand: it always gets the better side of a deal.
He supplies; refers to a merchant who contracted to deliver goods to the Temple.
A measure of volume (here, of flour).

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four' here means a LOWER price: four סאה for one סלע is cheaper than three סאה for one סלע. The bigger number means the buyer gets more flour for the same money.

phrases.english: [If he agreed to supply] at three, and [the price] came to stand at four –
phrases.notes: Three or four סאה of flour for one סלע coin. 'Four' means the flour got cheaper.

phrases.english: he supplies at four,
since the hand of the Temple treasury is on top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's explanation of מותר נסכים, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When prices drop, the supplier must give the הקדש the new, cheaper rate, because הקדש always gets the advantage.

steps.title: Each opinion has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting רבי חייא בר יוסף and another ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבי חייא בר יוסף, and a ברייתא was taught in line with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us it is about to bring one ברייתא supporting each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither opinion is rejected here. Each explanation of 'leftover libations' has its own support from a ברייתא, and the next two steps quote them.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: It is taught [in a baraita] in line with Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef,
it is taught [in a baraita] in line with Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that both explanations are stated, the גמרא announces support for each.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, quoted in the next steps

steps.title: ברייתא: what is done with liquid that overflows the measures
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains what happens to the overflow from the measuring cups. It goes with another offering that day; if it stays overnight it is disqualified; otherwise it is used for altar offerings, which are עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they do with these overflows of the measures? If there is another offering, they offer them with it. If they stayed overnight, they are disqualified by staying overnight. If not, they use them to keep the altar busy. And what is this 'keeping busy'? עולות: the meat goes to God, and the hides to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that supports רבי חייא בר יוסף. It deals with בירוצי מדות, the liquid that spills over the measuring cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the overflow of the measures as something that ends up being used for קיץ המזבח, the same use the משנה gives for מותר נסכים. That fits רבי חייא בר יוסף, who said 'leftover libations' means this overflow. The ברייתא also explains that these extra offerings are עולות: the meat is burned completely and the כהנים get the hides.

keyTerms.meaning: Overflows of the measuring cups: liquid that spills over the top when measuring.
Staying overnight; sacred items left past their time become disqualified.
'Summer fruit' of the altar: extra offerings brought to keep the altar from standing idle.
Burnt offerings, burned completely on the altar.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef:
These overflows of the measures,
what would they do with them?

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ זֶבַח אַחֵר – יַקְרִיבוּ עִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: If there is another offering – they offer them with it,
and if they stayed overnight – they are disqualified by staying overnight,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – מְקַיְּצִין בָּהֶן אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: and if not – they use them for the altar's 'summer fruit,'
phrases.notes: He means extra offerings bought with the overflow, so the altar is never left idle.

phrases.english: And this 'summer fruit,' what is it?
Burnt offerings – the meat to God,
and the hides to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first half of the announcement in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר יוסף's view that מותר נסכים means בירוצי מדות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing how the overflow of the measures is used for קיץ המזבח
steps.whyThisMatters: It also defines קיץ המזבח for the whole סוגיא: these are עולות, with the hides given to the כהנים.

steps.title: ברייתא: the supplier always delivers at the rate that favors the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. A supplier who agreed to four still gives four if the price rises to three, and one who agreed to three gives four if the price drops to four.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who takes it upon himself to supply fine flour at four, and the price rose to three, supplies at four. At three, and the price fell to four, he supplies at four, because the Temple treasury has the upper hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן. It states the full supplier rule in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whichever way the price moves, the הקדש gets the better rate. If prices rise, the supplier is held to his cheap promise. If prices fall, he must match the new cheap price. The second case is where the Temple ends up with extra flour.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes upon himself a commitment, here a supply contract.
Fine flour, used for מנחות.

phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
One who takes upon himself to supply fine flour at four,
and [the price] came to stand at three – he supplies at four.
phrases.notes: Here the flour got MORE expensive, but he is held to his original promise.

phrases.english: At three, and it came to stand at four – he supplies at four,
since the hand of the Temple treasury is on top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the second half of the announcement in step 2. It repeats the rule from step 1, now as part of a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that מותר נסכים is the extra flour from a price drop
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating the supplier rule

steps.title: The ברייתא ties the price-drop case to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that the price-drop case is exactly what the משנה meant by 'מותר נסכים לקיץ המזבח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned: leftover libations are for the altar's 'summer fruit'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא directly links its case to the words of our משנה. This is what makes it real support for רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not just give a rule that happens to fit רבי יוחנן. It says outright that this case is the 'leftover libations' of the משנה. The extra flour the הקדש gains when prices fall is sold and used for קיץ המזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover libations: the surplus that the משנה says goes to קיץ המזבח.
'And this is what we learned': links a case to a known משנה.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of מותר נסכים, and each has a ברייתא behind it. רבי חייא בר יוסף: the overflow of the measuring cups. רבי יוחנן: the extra the הקדש gains when a supplier's price drops. Both end up used for קיץ המזבח, which means עולות.

phrases.english: And this is what we learned:
Leftover libations are for the altar's 'summer fruit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 4 by tying it to the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא openly reads the משנה's 'מותר נסכים' as the price-drop surplus, which strongly supports רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The new משנה: which offerings need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: All communal and private offerings need נסכים except בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם. The חטאת and אשם of a מצורע do need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: All offerings, whether for the whole community or for one person, need נסכים. The exceptions are the בכור, the animal מעשר, the פסח, the חטאת and the אשם. But the חטאת and אשם of a מצורע do need נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and gives a general rule about which animal offerings must come with נסכים. It also lists the exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is broad: both communal and private offerings need נסכים. Five kinds of offerings are left out. Then there is an exception to the exception: a מצורע's חטאת and אשם bring נסכים even though ordinary ones do not.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour-and-oil offering plus the wine poured on the altar that go along with an animal offering
Offerings brought on behalf of the whole community
A single person (here, a private offering)
A firstborn male animal that is given as an offering
Here, the animal tithe: every tenth animal of the herd, brought as an offering
A person who had צרעת and brings offerings when he becomes pure

steps.whatToRemember: Rule: animal offerings need נסכים. Exceptions: בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת, אשם. Exception to the exception: the חטאת and אשם of a מצורע.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the מצורע's offerings stop being a חטאת and an אשם. They are still a חטאת and an אשם; they are simply a special case that does need נסכים.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
All offerings of the community and of the individual
require libations,
phrases.notes: "Libations" here means the full set: a flour-and-oil offering together with poured wine.

phrases.english: except for the firstborn and the animal tithe,
and the Paschal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
But the sin offering of a leper and his guilt offering
do require libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל קׇרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּיבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד טְעוּנִין נְסָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about price changes and leftover measures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All animal offerings need נסכים except בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם. The חטאת and אשם of a מצורע do need them.

steps.title: A מנחה does not need נסכים; an עולה does
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'ועשיתם אשה לה׳'. You might think anything burned on the altar needs נסכים, even a מנחה. The word 'עולה' shows that it is animal offerings that need them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And you will make a fire offering to ה׳.' You might think anything burned on the altar needs נסכים, even a מנחה. So the פסוק says 'עולה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts finding the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule. Its first move is to show that a מנחה does not need נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשה לה׳' alone could include anything burned on the altar, even a flour offering. The next word, 'עולה', narrows it to animal offerings like the עולה. This sets up the rest of the ברייתא, which adds other animal offerings one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: A fire offering, something burned on the altar for ה׳
The fires of the altar
"You might have thought": it brings up a possible wrong reading
"The פסוק teaches": it brings the word that settles the question
A flour offering
A burnt offering, burned completely on the altar

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And you will make a fire offering to the Lord"
One might think that anything that goes up on the fires
requires libations, even a meal offering?
The verse says: "A burnt offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts finding the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that animal offerings need נסכים (and a flour offering does not).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of 'ועשיתם אשה לה׳ עלה' (במדבר 15:3).

steps.title: שלמים and תודה are included
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זבח' adds שלמים, and the extra word 'או' in 'או זבח' adds תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that שלמים need נסכים? The פסוק says 'זבח'. Where do we learn that a תודה does? The פסוק says 'או זבח'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and adds more animal offerings that need נסכים, each one from a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עולה' alone would cover only burnt offerings. 'זבח' brings in שלמים. The extra word 'או' is read as adding the תודה, so it also needs נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, shared between the altar, the כהנים and the owner
A thanks offering
A slaughtered offering; here it refers to שלמים
"From where do we know?": a request for a source

phrases.english: From where do we learn peace offerings?
The verse says: "A sacrifice."
From where do we learn a thanks offering?
The verse says: "Or a sacrifice."
phrases.notes: The little word "or" is treated as extra, so it comes to add one more offering, the תודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 7 and adds שלמים and תודה to the עולה.
steps.raayaObject: שלמים and תודה need נסכים, as the משנה's general rule says.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'זבח' and 'או זבח' in במדבר 15:3.

steps.title: Required offerings are left out: only נדר and נדבה offerings need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: You might think that בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם are also included. The words 'לפלא נדר או בנדבה' show that only offerings that can come as a נדר or a נדבה need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should include even the בכור, the מעשר, the פסח, the חטאת and the אשם. So the פסוק says 'to fulfill a vow or as a gift'. An offering that comes as a נדר or נדבה needs נסכים. An offering that does not come as a נדר or נדבה does not need נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now finds the source for the משנה's list of exceptions. These are the five offerings that do not need נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'זבח' added animal offerings, every animal offering might seem to be included. The words 'נדר' and 'נדבה' limit it to offerings that can be brought by choice. בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם are always required and never come as a נדר or נדבה, so they are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Include; add to the rule
A vow: "I take on myself to bring an offering"
A gift offering: "This animal is an offering"
The Pesach offering
A sin offering
A guilt offering

steps.whatToRemember: The test for נסכים: can this kind of offering come as a נדר or a נדבה? If yes, it needs נסכים. Required offerings (בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת, אשם) do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the list of exceptions in the משנה. It still leaves open why a מצורע's חטאת and אשם do need נסכים.

phrases.english: One might think that I include even the firstborn,
and the animal tithe, the Paschal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering?
The verse says: "To fulfill a vow, or as a gift."
An offering that comes as a vow or gift requires libations;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה אֵין טָעוּן נְסָכִים.
phrases.english: one that does not come as a vow or gift does not require libations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 7 and 8 added offerings, this step sets the limit and leaves out the required ones.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's exceptions: בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם do not need נסכים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'לפלא נדר או בנדבה' in במדבר 15:3.

steps.title: Holiday-required offerings still need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: Since required offerings were left out, one might think the required holiday offerings (עולת ראייה and שלמי חגיגה) are also left out. The words 'או במועדיכם' teach that anything brought on the holidays needs נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned to leave out those required offerings. Should I also leave out the required offerings that are brought because of the holiday, on the holiday? Which are those? The עולת ראייה and the שלמי חגיגה. The פסוק says 'Or on your holidays': anything brought on your holidays needs נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a worry that its last rule went too far, and it uses a word in the פסוק to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said only offerings that can come as a נדר or נדבה need נסכים, so required offerings are out. But עולת ראייה and שלמי חגיגה are also required, so they might seem to be out too. The words 'או במועדיכם' put them back in.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt offering a person brings when coming to the בית המקדש on a רגל
The holiday peace offering brought on a רגל
One of the three pilgrimage holidays (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
A required offering, as opposed to a voluntary one
'On your holidays', the words in the פסוק that bring the holiday offerings back in

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 9. The holiday offerings are required, but they are still included, because the פסוק itself mentions the holidays.

phrases.english: We learned to leave out these,
phrases.notes: He means the offerings left out in step 9: בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: so should I also leave out the required offerings that come
because of the holiday, on the holiday?
And which are these?
Burnt offerings of appearance and holiday peace offerings.
The verse says: 'Or on your holidays,'
anything that comes on your holidays needs libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁמַע לְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ, אוֹצִיא אֶת חוֹבוֹת הַבָּאוֹת מֵחֲמַת הָרֶגֶל בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the exclusion from step 9 so that it does not cover required holiday offerings
steps.raayaObject: עולת ראייה and שלמי חגיגה need נסכים

steps.title: Holiday goat sin offerings do not need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: Now that required holiday offerings are included, one might think the holiday שעירי חטאת are included too. The פסוק 'וכי תעשה בן בקר' shows they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned to include these holiday offerings. Should I also include the goat sin offerings, since they too are brought as a requirement on the holiday? The פסוק says: 'And when you make a young bull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא worries that its last step now includes too much. It brings a new פסוק to limit it, and the next step explains how that פסוק works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If anything brought on a holiday needs נסכים, then the שעירי חטאת of the holiday should need them too. The ברייתא answers with the בן בקר פסוק but doesn't yet explain why it helps. That explanation comes in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as sin offerings among the holiday מוספין
'We learned to include', the opposite of מַשְׁמַע לְהוֹצִיא
A young bull

phrases.english: We learned to include these,
so should I also include the goat sin offerings,
since they also come as a requirement on the holiday?
The verse says: 'And when you make a young bull.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁמַע לְהָבִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ, אָבִיא שְׂעִירֵי חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps the inclusion from step 10 from also covering the שעירי חטאת
steps.raayaObject: שעירי חטאת of the holiday do not need נסכים

steps.title: How the בן בקר teaches the rule: a היקש
steps.stepSummary: The בן בקר was already covered by the general rule. It is singled out so that everything else can be compared to it: only offerings that can come as a נדר or נדבה, like a bull, need נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The young bull was already part of the general rule. So why was it singled out? So that we compare everything to it. A young bull is special because it can come as a נדר or a נדבה. So too, anything that can come as a נדר or a נדבה needs נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the בן בקר פסוק from step 11 leaves out the שעירי חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah mentions the bull separately even though it was already included. That extra mention teaches a comparison. A bull can be brought as a נדר or a נדבה, so only offerings that can come that way need נסכים. A חטאת can never come that way, so the שעירי חטאת are out. An עולה or שלמים can come that way, so the holiday עולת ראייה and שלמי חגיגה stay in.

keyTerms.meaning: Comparing one thing to another so they share the same law
It was part of the general rule and was singled out, so it teaches something about the whole group
Special, having a distinct feature

steps.whatToRemember: The test for נסכים is the type of offering: could it ever come as a נדר or נדבה? It does not depend on whether this specific one is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one test explains both results: the holiday עולות and שלמים are in, and the holiday שעירי חטאת are out.

steps.title: A bird עולה does not need נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה learns from 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' that the word 'עולה' only covers animal offerings, not a bird עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To make a pleasing smell to ה׳, from the cattle or from the flock.' Why does the פסוק say this? Since it said 'עולה', I might think that even a bird עולה is included. So the פסוק says 'from the cattle or from the flock.' These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a new question: what do the words 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' teach? רבי יאשיה says they leave out a bird עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עולה' could cover every burnt offering, even a bird. The words 'from the cattle or from the flock' limit נסכים to cattle and sheep or goats. This is a new limit, separate from the נדר and נדבה test, because a bird עולה can come as a נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering of a bird

steps.confusionAlert: A bird עולה passes the נדר and נדבה test, but it still doesn't need נסכים. That is because of this separate word in the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יונתן learns from the word 'זבח' that a bird needs no נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says the extra derivation is not needed. The word 'זבח' already shows that a bird needs no נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: You don't need that. The פסוק says 'זבח', and a bird is not called a זבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן gives a different source than רבי יאשיה did for why a bird עולה needs no נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה used 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' to limit the rule to animals. רבי יונתן says the word 'זבח' in the נסכים passage already limits it, because a bird offering is never called a זבח. Both reach the same law from different words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. The derivation just given is unnecessary.

steps.title: Then what are the words 'of the herd or of the flock' for?
steps.stepSummary: If 'זבח' already excludes birds, the ברייתא asks what the words 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'from the herd or from the flock'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן, still speaking in the ברייתא, asks a follow-up question about his own view. If 'זבח' already leaves out birds, the words רבי יאשיה used seem to have no job, and this sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה must teach something. Since רבי יונתן has moved the bird lesson onto 'זבח', he needs to find a new lesson for 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן'. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It introduces what follows from the previous claim.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying
"of the herd or of the flock"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 14. If 'זבח' does the excluding, the other words need a new purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' teach according to רבי יונתן.

steps.title: A person who vows a burnt offering may bring one type or both
steps.stepSummary: The words teach that someone who vows an עולה does not have to bring both cattle and sheep. He may bring one or both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק in ויקרא says 'from the herd and from the flock', you might think that someone who says 'I take upon myself an עולה' must bring from both. So the פסוק says 'from the herd or from the flock'. If he wants he brings one, and if he wants he brings two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' teaches that a person who vowed an עולה may choose cattle or flock. He does not need both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 1:2 says 'and', which could suggest that both types are required. The word 'או' (or) in the נסכים passage shows that either one alone fulfills the vow. That ends the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: I take upon myself an עולה. This is a vow that does not say which animal.
From both of them, cattle and flock

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן, 'זבח' excludes a bird from נסכים. 'מן הבקר או מן הצאן' teaches that a vowed עולה can be one animal of either type.

steps.title: Why does רבי יונתן need a פסוק, given his rule about 'יחדו'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יונתן. His own rule already says that two listed items are either-or unless the תורה writes 'יחדו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונתן, why does he need a פסוק? Doesn't he say that two things are not both required unless the פסוק spells it out with 'together'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the ברייתא's lesson according to רבי יונתן's own approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן holds that when the תורה lists two items, either one alone is enough unless the word 'יחדו' appears. By that rule, 'from the herd and from the flock' would already mean either one. So why does he need 'או' to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק for this?
Unless the פסוק spells it out for you
Together. This word shows that both items are required.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יונתן's rule works opposite to what you might expect. Two items joined by 'and' still count as either-or, unless the תורה adds 'יחדו'.

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Yonatan, why do I need a verse?
Doesn't he say: Not unless the verse spells out for you
"together"!
phrases.notes: He means that two things in a list are either-or, unless the תורה writes 'together'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lesson of step 16 using רבי יונתן's own rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that רבי יונתן needs 'או' to teach that one type of animal is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יונתן's rule about 'יחדו' already makes 'herd and flock' an either-or list, so the פסוק seems unneeded.

steps.title: The verse was still needed, because one might have thought otherwise
